verdict.rationale: First-party docs show Homebrew installs command-line tools and applications across macOS, Linux and WSL. Coverage comes through formulae with prebuilt bottles, casks for upstream binaries, and third-party taps, including software not packaged by Linux distros. Community users independently say brew has many more packages than MacPorts, updates versions quickly, and has better package support and maintenance than Nix, though some report version lag and no standard way to keep multiple language versions. Missing for 10: quantified registry size or activity metrics, evidence of timely version updates (one report of a tap skipping releases), and first-class multi-version installs.
